holidays.name: National Eat Your Vegetables Day
holidays.description: Today is the day to give broccoli a chance. Add a pile of carrots, a heap of greens, or one brave Brussels sprout to your plate. It's a nudge to put more color on your plate, and it lands in the middle of Fresh Fruit and Vegetables Month.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, and nobody seems to know who started it. It has become a fixture on June 17 and a handy excuse for parents everywhere.
holidays.funFact: Botanically speaking, tomatoes, cucumbers, and peppers are fruits. Plenty of people still count them toward their veggie goals today.

holidays.name: National Apple Strudel Day
holidays.description: Celebrate the flaky, cinnamon-spiced pastry with a slice of apple strudel. The dough is stretched paper-thin and rolled around apples, raisins, and sugar. Warm strudel with a scoop of vanilla ice cream makes a good dessert.
holidays.origin: Strudel is closely tied to Austrian and Central European baking, and the layered pastry traces back to the Ottoman-influenced kitchens of the Habsburg Empire. This food holiday is an unofficial observance, and its founder is unknown.
holidays.funFact: A well-made strudel dough is stretched so thin that you should be able to read a newspaper through it.

holidays.name: Take Your Cat to Work Day
holidays.description: This is a day for bringing your feline coworker to the office, or at least letting your cat supervise your video calls. Cats can contribute by sitting on keyboards, knocking pens off desks, and offering silent performance reviews.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, playful observance of unclear origin. It's a companion to the better-known Take Your Dog to Work Day, which comes a few days later.
holidays.funFact: Cats sleep about 12 to 16 hours a day, so your office cat would be the only team member who really maximizes nap time.
